Withdrawn —
Withdrawing is immediate and cannot be undone — a new verification and a new code would be required. Anyone checking the old code is told it was withdrawn, never that it did not exist.

When to withdraw without asking

  • A member removed for conduct — same day, before anything else.
  • A mark used to imply we vouch for someone's character.
  • A code appearing somewhere the member did not place it.
  • Any doubt about the identity you verified. Withdraw first, ask afterwards.

Relationship work

Formation, counsel and continuity — the three areas that concern a relationship a member is already in. Different work from a search, and it fails differently: quietly, and by being left alone too long.

Members in relationship work

Four active
B. VossFormation · month four Joint session on the 9th. Two conversations still unopened. Last session 12 days
J. AlbrightContinuity · fourth year Annual review due November. Nothing outstanding. Last contact 19 days
D. OkonjoCounsel · requested 16 Aug Asked for a session. Not yet answered. 3 days
R. Tanaka & partnerCounsel · session six Seen separately this month. Next joint session unscheduled. Last session 8 days

A search that stalls is visible. Relationship work that stalls is not — nobody complains, they simply stop coming. Treat fourteen days of silence here the way you would treat it on a search.

What is held separately

  • Counsel notes live with the counsel, not in the member's file.
  • Nothing said in counsel enters a profile, a brief, or a persona.
  • No advisor working on an introduction reads counsel material — including you, if you hold both.
  • Where both attend, each is also seen alone, always.
If you hold a member's search and their counsel at once, say so to them and offer to hand one of the two to a colleague. Most decline; the offer is the point.

When to hand it on

  • Clinical need — depression, addiction, anything requiring treatment rather than counsel.
  • Any indication that someone is unsafe. That is not a counsel matter.
  • A legal or financial dispute between the two of them.
  • Where you have formed a view you cannot set aside.
